observations: Torah #107 is a short rhetorical teaching about the futility of sexual desire, contrasting it with eating. The argument structure is entirely cause-and-effect (eitza): lust diminishes vitality, eating adds it, therefore lust is unnecessary except for procreation. No bechina (shared-nature) relationships are stated anywhere in the text. Without any bechina connections, the 3-node minimum threshold for a new package cannot be met. No new packages are proposed.
